title: When the Cover Turns
premise: Cyrus Montrose, a veteran crash investigator haunted by the unexplained loss of his family aboard Flight 447, is pulled into a live investigation when a passenger jet's digital records vanish mid-flight. He discovers a conspiracy inside the aviation safety apparatus itself: a cabal rewriting accident data to mask deliberate sabotage, with another attack already scheduled to look like mechanical failure. As Cyrus races to expose the plot, he must decide whether to trust Mara Voss, the insider who once buried the truth about row twelve, knowing loyalty and justice may demand opposite choices. In the end Cyrus stops the attack at terrible personal cost, exposes the conspiracy publicly, and finally learns what really happened to his family—choosing truth over the comfortable lies that kept him alive.
about_author: Freya Eastwick is a former airline operations analyst who spent a decade inside airport control rooms before turning to fiction full-time. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse in Cornwall, where she interviews pilots, investigators, and air traffic controllers for her research.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Fifteen years after losing his wife and daughter on Flight 447, Cyrus works a routine investigation into a runway overrun, methodically following protocol while flashbacks reveal how rules became his religion. A colleague mentions an anomaly: a flight currently airborne whose data feed has gone dark. The emotional beat is grief held at bay by procedure—and the first crack of dread.

chapters.title: The Silent Tail
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flight 882 lands safely, but every telemetry record, maintenance log, and passenger manifest has been wiped from three independent systems. Cyrus flags it officially and is quietly told to stand down by his own directorate. His instinct says cover-up; his training says coincidence. The beat is institutional gaslighting—the moment staying invisible stops being possible.

chapters.title: What Mara Knew
chapters.summary: Mara Voss's POV. Introduced as a senior safety-board analyst who signed off on the original Flight 447 report, Mara receives an anonymous warning that mirrors Cyrus's discovery. Flashbacks show she falsified one finding fifteen years ago under pressure. She reaches out to Cyrus, offering help she can't explain. The beat is guilt wearing competence as a mask.

chapters.title: Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Working off-record with Mara, Cyrus reconstructs Flight 882's passenger list from boarding-gate footage and finds a name that shouldn't exist: an engineer from the avionics firm that built 447's flight-data recorder. The man died two years ago—or someone wants the world to think so. The beat is the thrill of the hunt curdling into paranoia.

chapters.title: Rules Written in Pencil
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus presents his findings to his mentor, Director Hale, who reveals fragments of the conspiracy: a network inside the regulator that edits accident data to protect defense contracts tied to the avionics firm. Hale warns Cyrus he's being watched. That night his apartment is searched. The beat is betrayal—the institution he served becoming the threat.

chapters.title: The Fifteen-Year Lie
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara confesses to Cyrus: the 447 'accident' was sabotage, and she helped bury it to save her family from blackmail. Row twelve was targeted because a whistleblower sat there—Cyrus's wife. Cyrus's grief detonates into rage; he walks out. The beat is love against duty, shattered: the truth costs him the last comforting lie he had.

chapters.title: Countdown at Gate C
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Reconciling with Mara through shared purpose rather than forgiveness, they decode the ghost engineer's hidden files: a second sabotage is scheduled for tomorrow—a transatlantic flight carrying the conspiracy's last living witness, designed to fail over open ocean. They have hours, no authority, and every official channel compromised. The beat is desperate resolve.

chapters.title: Cleared for Departure
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Cyrus boards the flight posing as a deadheading inspector while Mara fights remotely to delay departure and reach the one honest federal prosecutor. Onboard, Cyrus identifies the saboteur—a maintenance contractor with a modified access panel—but security is tipped off and detains him. The beat is claustrophobic tension: trapped in a metal tube with the bomb and the blame.

chapters.title: Thirty Thousand Feet
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Handcuffed, Cyrus talks his way free as the saboteur triggers the failure sequence. In a brutal struggle down the aisle, Cyrus forces a diversion and manual override, and the plane lands hard but intact. The saboteur dies resisting arrest; the evidence survives in Cyrus's bloodied hands. The beat is survival at its true price—visible, wounded, and done hiding.

chapters.title: When the Cover Turns
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, epilogue six months later. Congressional hearings dismantle the network; Hale is arrested, Mara testifies and accepts consequences for 447. Cyrus visits the rebuilt memorial wall and adds his wife's real story beside her name. He takes a new post training honest investigators. The beat is resolution: truth chosen over safety, grief transformed into guardianship.
